concept.name: Know Sure Thing oscillator
concept.definition: Martin Pring's summed rate-of-change oscillator (Stocks & Commodities, 1992): four rate-of-change series over different periods, each SMA-smoothed, then combined with weights 1-2-3-4 so the longest cycle counts most.
concept.intuition: Instead of one momentum look-back, KST blends four cycles - short-term turns nudge it, but only broad multi-timeframe momentum swings really move it.
concept.mechanics: RCMA1 = SMA(ROC(10),10); RCMA2 = SMA(ROC(15),10); RCMA3 = SMA(ROC(20),10); RCMA4 = SMA(ROC(30),15); KST = 1xRCMA1 + 2xRCMA2 + 3xRCMA3 + 4xRCMA4, with a 9-period SMA signal line. Signals: signal-line crosses, centerline crosses, and trend-line breaks on the KST line itself.
concept.failure_modes: Unbounded, so no overbought/oversold levels exist, and signal-line crosses whipsaw - bearish crosses in strong uptrends often flag only slowing momentum, not reversal.
concept.misconceptions: The name promises certainty it cannot deliver - Pring himself stresses confirmation and warns that one parameter set does not fit all securities.
concept.example: If the four smoothed ROCs read +2, +3, +4, +5, then KST = 2 + 6 + 12 + 20 = +40.

citations.source: Pring's Know Sure Thing (KST) | ChartSchool | StockCharts.com
